mainTopic: A ברייתא explaining the פסוק about one who lies with his father's wife (ויקרא 20:11): who is liable, which women are included, which death penalty applies, and where the actual prohibition comes from.
overview: The amud opens with a long ברייתא that supports רבא's explanation of רבי יהודה. Reading the פסוקים about אשת אב, the ברייתא works out who is liable, that the punishment is סקילה, where the warning comes from, and how a mother who is not the father's wife is included. It ends by teaching that a man with his own mother is liable only as 'mother', not also as אשת אב. The גמרא then shows that the רבנן read 'ערות אביך' literally, as a ban on one's father that adds a second count to the general ban on a male. This matches רב יהודה, and רבא explains that the 'two counts' mean two קרבנות for a Jew who sinned by accident. Two views argue whether this fits רבי יהודה, and that argument depends on whether we punish based on a קל וחומר. Next the גמרא lists which words each side uses for the father's wife after the father's death, for her punishment, and for a mother who is not the father's wife. Along the way, אביי shows that רבי יהודה disagrees with the משנה about counting אשת איש. אביי also explains that כלתו and אשת בנו are one prohibition, not two. A new משנה then rules that relations with a male or with an animal are punished by סקילה and explains why the animal is killed too. The גמרא learns the law of a male from ויקרא 20:13 and its סקילה from the words 'דמיהם בם'.

steps.title: A ברייתא that supports רבא begins: 'a man' leaves out a minor
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a long ברייתא that matches רבא's view. Its first point is that the word 'איש' in the פסוק leaves out a קטן. The line that actually supports רבא comes at the end, in step 17.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רבא: the word 'man' in the פסוק excludes a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as support for what רבא just said. The first line teaches that the word 'איש' (a man) excludes a קטן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'תניא כוותיה' tells us this is backing for a view already stated, not a new argument. Because the פסוק says 'איש', a minor is not punished for this sin. The part that lines up with רבא is the ברייתא's last line (step 17): a man with his mother who is his father's wife is liable only as 'mother', not also as אשת אב.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא in agreement with him

steps.title: Father's wife is included whether or not she is his mother
steps.stepSummary: The words 'who lies with his father's wife' cover any wife of the father, both his own mother and a stepmother.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Who lies with his father's wife' means both a father's wife who is his mother and a father's wife who is not his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the next words of the פסוק. 'His father's wife' includes both his own mother and a stepmother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of 'אשת אביו' is any woman married to his father. So it includes his mother, who is married to his father, and a stepmother. This sets up the next question about a mother who is not his father's wife.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any wife of the father is included, whether or not she is the man's mother.

steps.title: What about his mother who is not his father's wife?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that a man is liable for his mother when she was never his father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the law for his mother who is not his father's wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks about a case the words 'his father's wife' do not cover: his mother who is not married to his father. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אשת אביו' require her to be his father's wife. So a mother who never married the father, for example a woman the father had a child with outside of marriage, is not covered by those words. The ברייתא needs another source for her.

phrases.english: His mother who is not his father's wife, from where do we know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a case the previous step's words do not include.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that makes a man liable for his mother even when she is not his father's wife.

steps.title: The extra words 'he uncovered his father's nakedness' teach a גזרה שוה
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'ערות אביו גלה' is not needed for its plain meaning. So it is free to be used for a גזרה שוה that adds his mother who is not his father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he has uncovered his father's nakedness.' These words are free to be used for a comparison and a גזרה שוה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the words 'ערות אביו גלה' are extra in the פסוק. Because they are extra, they are set aside to teach a גזרה שוה, and that brings in his mother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גזרה שוה can only be learned from words that are 'מופנה', meaning free and not needed for anything else. The פסוק already said 'אשת אביו', so 'ערות אביו גלה' adds nothing to the plain meaning. That makes it available for the גזרה שוה. The details of the comparison come later on the דף.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches; therefore the פסוק says
Free, not needed for its plain meaning

steps.confusionAlert: 'מופנה' does not mean the words are meaningless. It means they are not needed for their simple meaning here, so they can be used to teach something else.

steps.title: 'They shall be put to death' means stoning
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that the death penalty in this פסוק is סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They shall surely be put to death' means by stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the punishment and states that 'מות יומתו' here means סקילה. The proof comes in the next two steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מות יומתו' on its own only says there is a death penalty, not which kind. The ברייתא first gives the answer, סקילה, and then asks how we know it.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall surely be put to death
Stoning, the most severe of the four death penalties

phrases.english: "They shall surely be put to death" means by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who is included to which punishment applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The death penalty for אשת אב is סקילה.

steps.title: Why stoning and not another death penalty?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know it is סקילה rather than one of the other death penalties in the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it is by stoning, or is it really one of any of the death penalties stated in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא challenges its own claim. Since 'מות יומתו' does not name a method, maybe it is a different death penalty. This sets up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה has four kinds of court execution. Without a source, the words 'מות יומתו' could point to any of them. The ברייתא needs a proof that narrows it down to סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: The death penalties stated in the תורה

phrases.english: Do you say it is by stoning,

steps.title: Learned from אוב וידעוני through 'their blood is upon them'
steps.stepSummary: Both this פסוק and the פסוק about אוב וידעוני say 'דמיהם בם'. Since אוב וידעוני are punished with סקילה, so is this sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'their blood is upon them,' and about אוב and ידעוני it also says 'their blood is upon them.' Just as there it is stoning, so too here it is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a גזרה שוה. The same words, 'דמיהם בם', appear here and in the case of אוב וידעוני, where the פסוק clearly says סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק about אוב וידעוני the תורה says outright that they are stoned. Because the matching words 'דמיהם בם' appear in both places, the law of stoning carries over to אשת אב. This proves the ruling from step 5.

steps.whatToRemember: The punishment for אשת אב is סקילה, learned through the גזרה שוה of 'דמיהם בם' from אוב וידעוני.

steps.title: We know the punishment, but where is the warning?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that so far we have only the punishment. It asks where the actual prohibition (אזהרה) is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: We have heard the punishment; from where do we know the warning?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points out that a punishment alone is not enough. There also needs to be a warning, an אזהרה, so it asks where that comes from. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule assumed here is that the תורה does not punish unless it also warns. Chapter 20 of ויקרא gives the punishment, so the ברייתא looks for the actual prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: We have heard; we have learned

phrases.english: We have heard the punishment; the warning, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment to the prohibition behind it.

steps.title: The warning: 'Your father's nakedness you shall not uncover'
steps.stepSummary: The אזהרה comes from 'ערות אביך לא תגלה', and 'your father's nakedness' is read as your father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Your father's nakedness you shall not uncover.' 'Your father's nakedness' means your father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the source of the warning from ויקרא 18. It explains that 'ערות אביך' here refers to the father's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ערות אביך' could seem to be about the father himself. The ברייתא reads them as referring to the father's wife. This gives the warning that matches the punishment learned earlier.

keyTerms.meaning: Your father's nakedness; read here as your father's wife
You shall not uncover; do not have forbidden relations

steps.whatToRemember: For אשת אב, the punishment (סקילה) comes from ויקרא 20 and the warning comes from 'ערות אביך לא תגלה' in ויקרא 18.

steps.title: Does 'your father's nakedness' mean his wife or the father himself?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that 'ערות אביך' refers to the father's wife and not literally to the father.
steps.simpleTranslation: You say it means 'your father's wife.' But maybe it really means your father himself?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions the reading it just gave in Step 9. It is setting up the proof that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 read 'ערות אביך' as 'your father's wife.' But the plain words say 'your father's nakedness,' which could mean a forbidden act with the father himself. The ברייתא wants a source for its reading.

keyTerms.meaning: You say (opening a question about a proposed reading)
Literally, exactly as the words say

phrases.english: You say: "your father's wife,"

steps.title: The matching words prove the פסוק is about the father's wife
steps.stepSummary: The same phrase appears in the punishment פסוק, which clearly speaks of a wife, so here too it means the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here it says 'the nakedness of your father you shall not uncover,' and there it says 'he has uncovered his father's nakedness.' Just as there the פסוק speaks about a marriage, so too here it speaks about a marriage.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers by linking two פסוקים that share the words 'ערות אביך/אביו.' Since the second one is about a wife, the first one is too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishment פסוק in ויקרא 20 starts with 'a man who lies with his father's wife' and then says 'he has uncovered his father's nakedness.' So there the phrase clearly refers to the wife. The ברייתא carries that meaning back to the אזהרה in ויקרא 18.

steps.title: The prohibition covers every wife of the father
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק includes the father's wife whether she is the man's own mother or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this means: whether it is his father's wife who is his mother, or his father's wife who is not his mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא spells out how wide 'your father's wife' is. This also sets up the question in the next step about a case the פסוק has not yet covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the prohibition is about the father's wife, it does not matter whether she gave birth to this man. A stepmother is included just like his own mother. A mother who is not married to the father is not covered yet; the next two steps deal with her.

steps.title: What about his mother who is not his father's wife?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks for a source that a mother who is not married to the father is also forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that his mother who is not his father's wife is forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא points to a gap: 'father's wife' does not cover a mother who is not the father's wife. It asks for a source and sets up the next step.

steps.title: The source is 'the nakedness of your mother'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'ערות אמך לא תגלה' forbids one's mother even if she is not the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'The nakedness of your mother you shall not uncover.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a separate phrase in the same פסוק that forbids one's mother directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק says 'your mother' on its own, the prohibition depends on her being his mother, not on her being married to his father. So a mother who is not the father's wife is also forbidden. This gives the אזהרה for her.

steps.title: We have the prohibition, but where is the punishment?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא notes that so far only the אזהרה covers a mother who is not the father's wife, and asks for the source of the עונש.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only have the prohibition, where the verse treats his mother who is not his father's wife like his mother who is his father's wife. Where do we learn the punishment?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא admits a gap: the punishment פסוק speaks only about the father's wife. It asks where the punishment comes from and sets up the final step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 put both kinds of mother under the same אזהרה. But the punishment פסוק (ויקרא 20:11) says 'his father's wife,' so it seems to cover only a mother who is married to his father. The ברייתא needs a source for the punishment of the other mother.

steps.title: The same matching words carry the rule over to the punishment
steps.stepSummary: Using the same word-comparison, the ברייתא shows that the עונש, like the אזהרה, treats both kinds of mother alike.

steps.title: Liable as 'mother', not also as 'father's wife'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא closes: 'אמך היא' teaches that he is liable only for the איסור of his mother, not also for אשת אב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She is your mother': you make him liable because she is his mother, but you do not make him liable because she is his father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of the ברייתא. It says that when a man's mother is also his father's wife, he is liable only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12–16 showed that both kinds of mother are forbidden, with both an אזהרה and an עונש. Now the words 'אמך היא' limit the count. Even when she fits both categories, the חיוב is only for 'mother', so there is no second count for אשת אב. This is the line that supports רבא's explanation of רבי יהודה, announced in step 1.
steps.whatToRemember: According to this ברייתא, a man with his own mother, who is also his father's wife, gets only one חיוב: for 'mother'.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with step 21. Here the חיוב is limited to one count, but later 'ערות אביך' does add a second count, for relations with one's father.

phrases.english: "She is your mother" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:7

phrases.english: you make him liable because of his mother,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אָב.
phrases.english: and you do not make him liable because of father's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִמְּךָ הִיא מִשּׁוּם אִמּוֹ אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא after the עונש was derived in step 16, by limiting the number of counts.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Only one חיוב, as 'mother', even when she is also the father's wife.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read 'the nakedness of your father'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree with רבי יהודה, explain the words 'ערות אביך'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן — what do they do with 'the nakedness of your father'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other opinion. It asks how the רבנן explain 'ערות אביך' if they don't read it the way רבי יהודה does.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה used 'ערות אביך' for the father's wife. The רבנן do not accept that reading, so the words seem to have no job. The גמרא wants to know what those words teach for them.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages who disagree with רבי יהודה

phrases.english: And the Rabbis — "the nakedness of your father"?
phrases.notes: The question is short: what do the רבנן learn from these words, since they don't read them as the father's wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing רבי יהודה's ברייתא, the גמרא asks about the other side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the רבנן learn from 'ערות אביך'.

steps.title: It means literally: one's father
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן, 'ערות אביך' means exactly what it says: relations with one's father.
steps.simpleTranslation: Literally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in one word. The רבנן read 'ערות אביך' plainly, as a ban on relations with one's own father.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה turned 'your father' into 'your father's wife' through a comparison. The רבנן reject that comparison and keep the plain meaning: a male with his father.

phrases.english: Literally.
phrases.notes: He means the father himself, a male with a male, not the father's wife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן read 'ערות אביך' as a ban on relations with one's father.

steps.title: Isn't that already covered by 'with a male'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: relations with any male, including one's father, are already forbidden by 'ואת זכר'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this already learned from 'And with a male'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the רבנן. Why would the תורה need a special פסוק for the father if every male is already forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ואת זכר לא תשכב' already covers all males. A father is a male, so reading 'ערות אביך' literally seems to make it extra, with nothing new to teach.

keyTerms.meaning: It is derived, it comes out from

phrases.english: Isn't this derived from "And with a male"?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 19 as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's literal reading of 'ערות אביך'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'ואת זכר' already forbids all males, so a separate ban for the father adds nothing.

steps.title: To make him liable twice
steps.stepSummary: The extra פסוק adds a second count, so with his father he is liable twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: To make him liable for two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the special פסוק for the father is not extra. It adds a second count of liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relations with one's father break two separate איסורים: 'male' and 'father'. So if done by mistake, he brings two קרבנות חטאת, not one.

phrases.english: To make him liable two for it.
phrases.notes: Two counts: one for being a male and one for being his father, which means two חטאות if done by mistake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the פסוק a new job: an extra count of liability.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'ערות אביך' seemed to repeat 'ואת זכר' for no reason.
steps.terutzMaskana: It adds a second, separate חיוב for the father.

steps.title: Support from רב יהודה: two counts for father and father's brother
steps.stepSummary: This matches רב יהודה, who said one who has relations with his father, or with his father's brother, is liable twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is like רב יהודה, for רב יהודה said: A gentile who has relations with his father is liable twice; one who has relations with his father's brother is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the 'two counts' idea is not new. רב יהודה already said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה rules that relations with one's father bring two counts, matching step 21. He adds the father's brother, who is also forbidden by his own פסוק ('ערות אחי אביך') on top of 'male'.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is like רב יהודה

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן, 'ערות אביך' is literal and adds a second count to 'ואת זכר'. רב יהודה rules the same way, two counts, for the father and for the father's brother.

phrases.english: And this is in line with רב יהודה,
for רב יהודה said:
A gentile who has relations with his father –
is liable for two,
one who has relations with his father's brother –
is liable for two.
phrases.notes: The father's brother has his own ban in the פסוק 'ערות אחי אביך', on top of 'male', so again two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 21 with a known ruling.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one who has relations with his father is liable for two counts.

steps.title: רבא: the ruling is about a Jew who sinned by accident
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רב יהודה's ruling is about a Jew acting בשוגג who brings two קרבנות, and the word 'gentile' was just a polite way of speaking.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It makes sense that רב יהודה's ruling is about a Jew who did this by accident, and it is about bringing offerings. When he said 'gentile,' that was just a polite way of putting it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains what 'liable twice' in רב יהודה's ruling really means and who it is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's wording began with 'a gentile who...'. רבא says it really means a Jew who sinned without knowing, so 'twice' means two חטאת offerings. He used the word 'gentile' so he would not pin such an ugly sin on a Jew.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / it stands to reason
An offering (here, a חטאת brought for an accidental sin)
A refined or polite way of speaking (a euphemism)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the ruling is really about non-Jews. רבא says the word 'gentile' was only polite language, and the case is about a Jew.

phrases.english: Rava says:
It stands to reason that the statement of Rav Yehuda
is about a Jew acting unknowingly,
and it is about an offering.
And the fact that he said "gentile"
phrases.notes: רב יהודה's ruling opened with the words 'a gentile who has relations with his father.'

phrases.english: is just a refined way of speaking.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מִסְתַּבְּרָא מִילְּתָא דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the case and meaning behind רב יהודה's ruling quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה's 'liable twice' is about a Jew who sinned בשוגג and brings two קרבנות. 'Gentile' was polite wording.

steps.title: Proof: you cannot execute someone twice
steps.stepSummary: רבא proves his reading: a real gentile would get the death penalty, and 'twice' would mean nothing because no one can be killed twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think it means an actual gentile, what is his punishment? Death! Can you kill him twice?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his reading by showing that the literal reading makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew who commits this sin gets the death penalty. Being 'liable twice' would change nothing for him, since a person can only die once. So 'twice' only makes sense for a Jew bringing two קרבנות for an accidental sin.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think / if it enters your mind

phrases.english: For if it enters your mind that it means an actual gentile,
what is his punishment?
Death!
Will you kill him with two deaths?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind רבא's reading in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That רב יהודה's ruling is about a Jew בשוגג, not a real gentile.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Simple logic: a death penalty cannot be given twice, so 'twice' has to mean two קרבנות.

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same ruling
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רב יהודה: relations with one's father, or with one's father's brother, make a person liable twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: One who has relations with his father is liable twice. One who has relations with his father's brother is liable twice.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רב יהודה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives רב יהודה's ruling the backing of a תנאי source. In each case there are two prohibitions: the general ban on relations with a male, and a family-relation prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a support)

phrases.english: It is also taught this way:
One who has relations with his father is liable twice,

phrases.aramaic: הַבָּא עַל אֲחִי אָבִיו – חַיָּיב שְׁתַּיִם.
phrases.english: one who has relations with his father's brother is liable twice.
phrases.notes: The second count for the uncle comes from ויקרא 18:14.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב יהודה's ruling.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's ruling that one is liable twice for his father and for his father's brother.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא with the same wording.

steps.title: One view: the ברייתא does not follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: Some say the ברייתא does not fit רבי יהודה, because he reads 'ערות אביך' as being about the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: this ברייתא is not in line with רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא the ברייתא follows, and gives the first answer: not רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads 'ערות אביך' as talking about the father's wife. So for him there is no extra prohibition for one's father. That leaves only the general ban on a male, so the father case would be liable only once. The ברייתא therefore must follow the רבנן.

phrases.english: Some say:
this is not in line with Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out which opinion the ברייתא from step 25 follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, not רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Another view: the ברייתא can fit רבי יהודה too
steps.stepSummary: Others say the ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה, because he learns the father case through a קל וחומר from the father's brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: You can even say it follows רבי יהודה, and he learns it through a קל וחומר from the father's brother.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion says the ברייתא can fit רבי יהודה after all. It sets up a קל וחומר that the next step spells out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not get the extra count for one's father from the פסוק 'ערות אביך'. But he can still reach it by logic, starting from the father's brother, where the extra count is clear.

keyTerms.meaning: A logical argument from a lighter case to a stronger one
He derives it, he brings it

phrases.english: And some say:
you can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda,

phrases.aramaic: וּמַיְיתֵי לַהּ בְּקַל וָחוֹמֶר מֵאֲחִי אָבִיו.
phrases.english: and he derives it through a kal vachomer from the father's brother.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with step 26 and fits the ברייתא into רבי יהודה's view.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: logic (קל וחומר) instead of a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי יהודה reads 'ערות אביך' as the father's wife, he cannot hold that one is liable twice for his father.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה can still hold liable twice, learning it through a קל וחומר from the father's brother.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה, who learns the extra count for one's father through a קל וחומר from the father's brother.

steps.title: The קל וחומר spelled out
steps.stepSummary: If one is liable twice for the father's brother, who is only the father's relative, then surely he is liable twice for the father himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: If for the father's brother, who is only a relative of his father, one is liable twice, then for his father himself, all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the קל וחומר step by step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The uncle is forbidden only because he is connected to the father. The father himself is the main person behind that connection. So whatever extra count applies to the uncle must apply to the father even more.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: the 'twice' is two קרבנות for a Jew who sinned by accident. The ברייתא agrees. It surely fits the רבנן, and according to the second view it fits רבי יהודה too, through a קל וחומר from the father's brother.

phrases.english: Now if his father's brother,
who is only his father's relative,
one is liable twice,
for his father, is it not all the more so?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמָה אֲחִי אָבִיו, דְּקוּרְבָה דְּאָבִיו הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the קל וחומר introduced in step 27.
steps.raayaObject: That even according to רבי יהודה one is liable twice for relations with his father.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from the father's brother, who is only a relative through the father.

steps.title: The two readings match the argument of אביי and רבא
steps.stepSummary: The two readings of רבי יהודה disagree about whether we punish based on a קל וחומר, which is the same argument as אביי and רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The two readings argue about the same thing that אביי and רבא argue about. One holds that we punish based on a קל וחומר. The other holds that we do not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real reason behind the two readings of רבי יהודה from steps 26 and 27.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second reading said a person is liable twice for his father because of a קל וחומר from the father's brother. That only works if a קל וחומר is strong enough to punish. The first reading holds that a קל וחומר cannot create a punishment, so it says the ברייתא does not fit רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: we punish based on a קל וחומר
we do not punish based on a קל וחומר

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'דין' does not mean a court case or a law. It means a קל וחומר, a logical 'how much more so' argument.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the disagreement about רבי יהודה's view is not just about reading a ברייתא. It depends on a big rule: can a קל וחומר be used to punish?

phrases.english: And they disagree about the dispute of Abaye and Rava.
phrases.notes: 'They' means the two readings of רבי יהודה from the last few steps.

phrases.english: One Sage holds: we punish based on a logical inference,
phrases.notes: This is the second reading, the one that used the קל וחומר from the father's brother.

phrases.aramaic: וּמַר סָבַר: אֵין עוֹנְשִׁין מִן הַדִּין.
phrases.english: And one Sage holds: we do not punish based on a logical inference.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the root of the disagreement between the two readings in steps 26-28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two readings of רבי יהודה reflect the dispute over whether we punish based on a קל וחומר.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן learn the warning about a father's wife?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which פסוק the רבנן use for the warning against relations with a father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, where do they learn the warning against a father's wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the רבנן, who argue with רבי יהודה, and asks for their source. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה learns the warning about a father's wife from 'ערות אביך'. The רבנן read 'ערות אביך' as being about the father himself. So the גמרא asks where they learn the warning about the father's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: a warning, a prohibition written in the תורה
from where do they learn it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
the prohibition of his father's wife, from where do they derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, אַזְהָרָה לְאֵשֶׁת אָבִיו מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי יהודה's view to ask about the רבנן's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק the רבנן use for the warning about a father's wife.

steps.title: The רבנן learn it from 'your father's wife'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn the warning from the words 'ערות אשת אביך לא תגלה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: They learn it from 'The nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the רבנן use the clear words of the פסוק that mention the father's wife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק says 'אשת אביך', your father's wife, outright. So the רבנן have a direct source and do not need 'ערות אביך' for the father's wife.

keyTerms.meaning: you shall not uncover, meaning do not have forbidden relations

phrases.english: They derive it
from: "The nakedness of your father's wife you shall not uncover."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:8

steps.triggerLanguage: נָפְקָא לְהוּ מֵ״עֶרְוַת אֵשֶׁת אָבִיךָ לֹא תְגַלֵּה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn it from 'ערות אשת אביך לא תגלה'.

steps.title: רבי יהודה uses that phrase for after the father's death
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה needs 'ערות אשת אביך' to teach that the father's wife stays forbidden even after the father dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהודה? He needs that phrase for the warning against a father's wife after the father's death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what רבי יהודה does with the phrase 'אשת אביך', since he already has 'ערות אביך' for the father's wife, and it answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה already learned the basic warning from 'ערות אביך'. So he uses 'אשת אביך' to add something new. Even after the father is gone, his wife stays forbidden to the son.

keyTerms.meaning: he needs it for something else

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: The question is left unsaid: what does he do with 'your father's wife', since he learns the warning from 'your father'?

phrases.english: That verse is needed by him
for the prohibition of his father's wife after the father's death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Checks how רבי יהודה uses the phrase the רבנן just used.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה uses 'אשת אביך' to forbid the father's wife even after the father's death.

steps.title: The רבנן learn 'after death' from the end of the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן learn that the father's wife stays forbidden after his death from the end of the פסוק, 'ערות אביך היא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן? They learn that rule from the end of the פסוק: 'It is your father's nakedness.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where the רבנן learn the 'after death' rule, since they used the first phrase for the basic warning, and it answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the father's wife is forbidden after the father dies. They only argue about which words teach it. The רבנן take it from the closing words 'ערות אביך היא'.
steps.whatToRemember: The basic warning against a father's wife and the 'after death' rule are agreed by both sides. They differ in which words of ויקרא 18:8 teach each one. They also have real disagreements: for the רבנן, 'ערות אביך' is a separate ban on one's father, and the next steps show that רבי יהודה does not count אשת איש together with אשת אב.

phrases.english: And the Rabbis?
That is derived from the end of the verse:
"It is your father's nakedness."
phrases.notes: The same פסוק, ויקרא 18:8. 'Your father's wife' is still called 'his', even after he dies.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers how the רבנן cover the 'after death' rule that רבי יהודה learned in step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn the 'after death' rule from 'ערות אביך היא'.

steps.title: What רבי יהודה learns from 'ערות אביך היא'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה uses 'ערות אביך היא' to teach that a man with his father's wife is liable only for אשת אב, not for אשת איש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does רבי יהודה do with those words? He needs them to teach: you make him liable because she is his father's wife, but you do not make him liable because she is a married woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The רבנן just used 'ערות אביך היא' to teach that she stays forbidden after the father dies, so the גמרא asks what רבי יהודה does with those words. It answers that he uses them to teach that the man is liable for only one sin, not two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every word of the תורה has to teach something. רבי יהודה already learned the after-death rule from other words, so 'ערות אביך היא' is free to teach something else. It teaches that the sin counts only as אשת אב, even though she is also a married woman.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (to teach something else)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
phrases.notes: Meaning: what does he learn from 'ערות אביך היא', the words the רבנן just used?

phrases.english: He needs that for this:
You make him liable because she is his father's wife,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מְחַיְּיבוֹ מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת אִישׁ.
phrases.english: but you do not make him liable because she is a married woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks and answers what רבי יהודה does with the words the רבנן used in step 33.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does רבי יהודה learn from 'ערות אביך היא'?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He learns that the man is liable only for אשת אב, not also for אשת איש.

steps.title: A משנה says he is liable for both
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that he is liable for both אשת אב and אשת איש, and רבי יהודה is not recorded as disagreeing.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: one who has relations with his father's wife is liable for her because she is his father's wife and because she is a married woman, whether during his father's lifetime or after his father's death. And רבי יהודה does not disagree there!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave by quoting a משנה. The משנה says he is liable for two sins, and nobody records רבי יהודה disagreeing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 34 said that in רבי יהודה's view he is liable only for אשת אב. The משנה counts both אשת אב and אשת איש, and it names no disagreement. So it looks like רבי יהודה agrees he is liable for both, and that contradicts step 34.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn (in a משנה)?

steps.confusionAlert: The 'after his father's death' part applies only to the אשת אב count. Once the father dies she is no longer a married woman.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in a משנה:
One who has relations with his father's wife
is liable for her because she is his father's wife
and because she is a married woman,
whether during his father's lifetime
or after his father's death,
and Rabbi Yehuda does not disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 34's claim about רבי יהודה's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה holds he is not liable for אשת איש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה with no recorded disagreement counts both sins, so רבי יהודה seems to agree he is liable for both.

steps.title: אביי: he disagrees in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that רבי יהודה's disagreement is recorded in a ברייתא, even though the משנה leaves it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: He disagrees in a ברייתא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. רבי יהודה does disagree with the משנה, and the disagreement is written in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fact that the משנה does not mention a disagreement does not prove that everyone agrees. Another source, a ברייתא, records רבי יהודה disagreeing. So step 34's reading of רבי יהודה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching of the תנאים that was not included in the משנה

phrases.english: Abaye said:
He disagrees in a ברייתא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 35.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The silent source is matched against another source that records the disagreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the משנה's silence meant רבי יהודה agrees he is liable for both sins.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה disagrees in a ברייתא, so his view stands: he is liable only for אשת אב.
steps.whatToRemember: In רבי יהודה's view, relations with a father's wife count only as אשת אב, not also as אשת איש. The משנה does not mention his disagreement, but a ברייתא does.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן get the punishment after the father's death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the רבנן's source for punishing someone with his father's wife after the father dies, since only רבי יהודה has a גזירה שוה for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, where do they get the punishment for his father's wife after the father's death? It works well for רבי יהודה, who brings it through a גזירה שוה. But the רבנן, where do they get it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves from the warning to the punishment. It asks where the רבנן learn the punishment for a father's wife after the father has died, and it sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far the גמרא showed where the רבנן get the warning (step 33). The תורה also needs a source for the punishment. רבי יהודה has one through a גזירה שוה, but the רבנן do not use it, so they need a different source.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do they get it from?
It works well for (one side), but...
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two פסוקים

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
the punishment for his father's wife after death,
where do they get it from?
It works well for Rabbi Yehuda:
he brings it through a גזירה שוה,
but the Rabbis, where do they get it from?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, עוֹנֶשׁ דְּאֵשֶׁת אָבִיו לְאַחַר מִיתָה מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the רבנן's source for the warning (step 33) to their source for the punishment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The רבנן's source for the punishment for a father's wife after the father's death.

steps.title: The רבנן use 'ערות אביו גלה' for the punishment after the father's death
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן take the phrase that רבי יהודה uses for his גזירה שוה and use it to punish relations with the father's wife after the father has died.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן can answer you: the phrase 'he has uncovered his father's nakedness,' which רבי יהודה uses for a גזירה שוה, is used by the רבנן to teach the punishment for the father's wife after the father's death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the previous step. It shows where the רבנן get the punishment for being with the father's wife after the father dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides use the same words of the פסוק, but for different jobs. רבי יהודה uses them for a גזירה שוה. The רבנן use them to teach that the punishment still applies after the father's death. So the רבנן are not left without a source.

keyTerms.meaning: They can say to you (introduces how the other side would answer)
He takes it out, meaning he uses this פסוק to learn something
A teaching learned from the same word appearing in two places in the תורה
After death (here, after the father has died)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common pattern in the גמרא: when one opinion uses a phrase for one teaching, the other opinion usually uses the same phrase for a different teaching.

phrases.english: They can say to you:
phrases.notes: 'They' means the רבנן, answering the question from the last step.

phrases.english: that phrase, "he has uncovered his father's nakedness,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:11

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַפֵּיק לַהּ רַבִּי יְהוּדָה לִגְזֵירָה שָׁוָה,
phrases.english: which Rabbi Yehuda uses for a verbal analogy,
they use it
for the punishment for his father's wife after the father's death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן learn the punishment after the father's death from 'ערות אביו גלה', the same phrase that רבי יהודה uses for his גזירה שוה.

steps.title: Where do the רבנן get the punishment for a mother who is not the father's wife?
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן have used up 'ערות אביו גלה', so the גמרא asks where they learn the punishment for relations with one's mother when she is not the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן: where do they learn the punishment for his mother who is not his father's wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question. The phrase the רבנן had has now been used for something else, so where do they learn this other case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is a mother who was never married to the father. Here only the prohibition of 'mother' applies, not אשת אב. The רבנן need a separate source for her punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: His mother who is not his father's wife (she was never married to his father)
From where do they know it?

phrases.english: And the Rabbis:
the punishment for his mother who is not his father's wife,
from where do they derive it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, עוֹנֶשׁ לְאִמּוֹ שֶׁאֵינָהּ אֵשֶׁת אָבִיו מְנָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 38 used up the רבנן's phrase, so the גמרא now asks what source is left for the mother case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for punishing relations with one's mother when she is not the father's wife, according to the רבנן.

steps.title: רב שישא: 'אמך היא' includes any mother
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי says the words 'she is your mother' put a mother who is not the father's wife in the same category as a mother who is the father's wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שישא son of רב אידי said: The פסוק says 'she is your mother.' The פסוק made his mother who is not his father's wife the same as his mother who is his father's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: רב שישא answers the question. He points to the words 'אמך היא' in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'היא' stresses that she is your mother no matter what, even without a marriage to the father. So whatever punishment applies to a mother who is the father's wife also applies to a mother who is not.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק made her (treated her the same as)

steps.whatToRemember: For the רבנן: 'ערות אביו גלה' teaches the punishment after the father's death, and 'אמך היא' covers a mother who was never the father's wife.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי:
phrases.english: Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
The verse states: "She is your mother."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:7

phrases.english: The verse made his mother
who is not his father's wife
like his mother who is his father's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי: אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 39.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'אמך היא' treat a mother who is not the father's wife the same as a mother who is.

steps.title: Why not a third liability for 'his son's wife'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה makes one who is with his כלה liable twice: as כלתו and as אשת איש. The גמרא asks why he is not also liable a third time for אשת בנו.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'One who has relations with his daughter-in-law' and so on. Then let him also be liable because she is his son's wife!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה. It challenges the משנה for leaving out a third liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names her twice, first as 'your כלה' and then as 'your son's wife.' The גמרא suggests these might be two separate prohibitions. If so, the משנה should have listed three liabilities, not two.

keyTerms.meaning: And let him also be liable

phrases.english: One who has relations with his daughter-in-law, etc.
And let him also be liable
because she is his son's wife!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַבָּא עַל כַּלָּתוֹ כּוּ׳. וְלִחַיַּיב נָמֵי מִשּׁוּם אֵשֶׁת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the אשת אב discussion and starts on the משנה's next case, כלתו.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one who is with his כלה is liable only twice (כלתו and אשת איש).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק also calls her 'אשת בנו'. If that is a separate prohibition, there should be a third liability.

steps.title: אביי: 'כלתו' and 'אשת בנו' are the same prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the פסוק starts with 'כלתך' and ends with 'אשת בנך' to show that these are one and the same, not two prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The פסוק opens with his daughter-in-law and ends with his son's wife. This teaches you that his daughter-in-law is the same as his son's wife.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers the challenge. The second name in the פסוק only explains the first one; it is not a new prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אשת בנך' tells us who the 'כלה' is: the wife of your son. It describes the same woman and the same prohibition. So there is no third liability, and the משנה is correct.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תורה lists two separate sins here. The two names describe one woman and one prohibition.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
The verse opened with his daughter-in-law
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:15

phrases.english: and ended with his son's wife,
to tell you: this is his daughter-in-law,
and this is his son's wife.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: פָּתַח הַכָּתוּב בְּכַלָּתוֹ וְסִיֵּים בְּאֵשֶׁת בְּנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק: the second phrase defines the first and does not add to it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'כלתו' and 'אשת בנו' are two separate prohibitions, which would mean three liabilities.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are one prohibition, so there are only two liabilities, as the משנה says.

steps.title: New משנה: stoning for relations with a male or with an animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a man who has relations with a male or with an animal, and a woman who has relations with an animal, are punished by stoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One who has relations with a male, or with an animal, and a woman who brings an animal upon herself, are put to death by stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists more sins whose punishment is סקילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three cases here: a man with a male, a man with an animal, and a woman with an animal. All three receive the same punishment, סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, a form of בית דין execution

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who has relations with a male,
or with an animal,
and the woman who brings an animal upon herself,
are executed by stoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא on the previous one ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Relations with a male, or with an animal (by a man or a woman), are punished by סקילה.

steps.title: If the person sinned, why is the animal punished?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks why the animal is also stoned, since an animal cannot sin.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the person sinned, what sin did the animal do?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה raises a question. It is setting up the explanations that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is put to death together with the person, but an animal has no free choice and cannot sin. So the punishment needs a reason.

phrases.english: If the person sinned,
how did the animal sin?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אָדָם חָטָא, בְּהֵמָה מֶה חָטְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind stoning the animal in the case of step 43.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason the animal is stoned even though it did not sin.

steps.title: First reason: the animal caused a person to stumble
steps.stepSummary: The animal is stoned because it brought disaster to a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since a person came to disaster through it, the פסוק said it should be stoned.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first answer to the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animal is not being punished for a sin. It is killed because it was the means through which a person fell into a terrible sin.

phrases.english: Rather, because there came to a person
a disaster through it,
therefore the verse said it shall be stoned.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְפִי שֶׁבָּאָה לְאָדָם תַּקָּלָה עַל יָדָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is stoned because it caused a person to sin.

steps.title: Second reason: to protect the dead person's memory
steps.stepSummary: The animal is stoned so that people will not point at it in the market and recall the person who was stoned because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation: so that the animal should not walk through the market while people say, 'This is the one because of which so-and-so was stoned.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second, different answer to the same question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This reason looks at the person's honor. If the animal stays alive, people seeing it would keep remembering his shameful sin.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה gives two reasons the animal is stoned: it caused a person's downfall, and keeping it alive would shame the person's memory.

phrases.english: Another explanation:
so that the animal should not pass through the marketplace
while people say, "This is the one
because of which so-and-so was stoned."

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּבָר אַחֵר: שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא בְּהֵמָה עוֹבֶרֶת בַּשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 44, alongside the answer in step 45.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is stoned so that it will not remind people of the person's shameful death.

steps.title: Where do we learn the law of relations with a male?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source in the תורה of the משנה's ruling about relations with a male.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: A male, from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion of the משנה by asking where the תורה teaches the law about relations with a male. This question sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that a man who has relations with a male is stoned. The גמרא wants a פסוק that shows both the prohibition and the punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: GEMARA: A male — from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה quoted in step 43.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for the prohibition and death penalty of relations with a male.

steps.title: The ברייתא reads the פסוק word by word
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ויקרא 20:13. 'Man' excludes a minor sinner, 'a male' includes an adult or minor partner, and 'lyings of a woman' teaches two kinds of relations with a woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the רבנן taught: 'A man' excludes a minor. 'Who lies with a male' means whether the male is an adult or a minor. 'Lyings of a woman' teaches that there are two kinds of lying with a woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The ברייתא reads the פסוק about a male one phrase at a time and pulls a separate law out of each phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'man' limits who is punished: only an adult, not a קטן. The partner, called 'a male', can be any age. The plural form 'lyings' shows that relations with a woman come in two kinds, and both count for punishment.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two people. The minor who is excluded is the one doing the act (the 'man'). The male partner can be any age.

phrases.english: As the Sages taught:
"A man" — this excludes a minor,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:13

phrases.english: "who lies with a male"
— whether an adult or a minor,
"the lyings of a woman" —
the verse tells you
that there are two kinds of lying with a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 47 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 20:13 is the source. Its words define who is liable, include a partner of any age, and show two kinds of relations with a woman.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a teaching phrase that also teaches about itself
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל observes that 'lyings of a woman' came to teach about a male, but it ends up teaching a law about women as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל said: This phrase comes to teach, and it turns out that it is taught.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל comments on the phrase 'lyings of a woman.' He points out that it does a double job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase was written to teach about relations with a male, by comparing it to a woman. But from that same comparison we also learn something new about women: there are two kinds of forbidden relations with them. So the phrase that 'teaches' ends up also being 'taught.'

keyTerms.meaning: And turns out to be taught

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael said:
This comes to teach,
and it turns out to be taught.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה בָּא לְלַמֵּד וְנִמְצָא לָמֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on how the last phrase of step 48 works.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The phrase 'lyings of a woman' teaches about a male and also teaches the law of two kinds of relations with a woman.

steps.title: Which death penalty: is it really סקילה?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says 'they shall surely be put to death' means סקילה. It then asks how we know it is not one of the other death penalties.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'They shall surely be put to death' means by stoning. Do you say by stoning, or perhaps it is one of the other deaths mentioned in the תורה?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says the death penalty here is סקילה. It then asks how we know this, which sets up the proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק only says 'they shall surely be put to death' and does not say how. The תורה has several kinds of death penalty, so a source is needed to show that this one is stoning.

keyTerms.meaning: They shall surely be put to death
Do you say (introduces a challenge to prove a point)

phrases.english: "They shall surely be put to death" — by stoning.
Do you say by stoning,
or is it perhaps by one
of all the deaths stated in the Torah?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בִּסְקִילָה אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who is liable to which death penalty applies.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the unspecified death penalty in the פסוק is סקילה.

steps.title: Proof from 'their blood is upon them'
steps.stepSummary: The same words, 'their blood is upon them,' appear here and by אוב and ידעוני. Those are stoned, so this sin is also punished with סקילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It says here 'their blood is upon them,' and it says by אוב and ידעוני 'their blood is upon them.' Just as there it is stoning, so too here it is stoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves that the punishment is stoning. It does this by matching the same words in two different פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a גזירה שוה, which means learning one case from another because the תורה uses the same words in both. The תורה clearly says that אוב and ידעוני are stoned (ויקרא 20:27). Because both פסוקים say 'their blood is upon them,' relations with a male also gets סקילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Two kinds of forbidden sorcery (calling up the dead)
Just as there, so too here (the language of a גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: Relations with a male: the פסוק is ויקרא 20:13, a minor is not liable, the partner can be any age, and the death penalty is סקילה. We learn the סקילה from 'their blood is upon them' by אוב and ידעוני.

phrases.english: It is stated here, "their blood is upon them,"
and it is stated about a necromancer and a sorcerer, "their blood is upon them."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 20:27, where the פסוק says outright that they are stoned.

phrases.english: Just as there it is by stoning,
